sowhat.text: Financing stays costly with the 10-year at 5.12% and a December hike mostly priced, but high yield spreads near 323 bp show credit is open. A tech and AI sell-off can slow stock-funded deals, while energy and power asset sales keep getting done.

pitch: Stocks sold off hard Monday. The S&P 500 fell 1.9 percent to about 7,417 and the Nasdaq dropped 2.5 percent, led by Nvidia, which slid after its CEO left and the US tightened limits on Chinese access to advanced chips. Oil fell about 3 percent, with Brent near 92 dollars, on expectations of a supply surplus. The 10-year eased 3 basis points to 5.12 percent, and markets still lean toward a December Fed hike. On deals, ECP closed its EnergySolutions buyout, Strathcona is buying Greenfire for roughly 2.7 to 2.9 billion including debt, and NRG is selling six gas plants to LS Power for 4 billion, with Barclays advising NRG.

quiz.q: Where did Brent crude settle on Monday 16 Nov?
Why did the Nasdaq fall about 2.5% on Monday 16 Nov?
quiz.a: Nvidia fell 4.1% after CEO Jensen Huang's exit, and new Commerce limits on Chinese remote access to advanced chips hit chip stocks broadly.

quiz.q: Who was lead financial adviser to Strathcona on buying Greenfire, and what is the deal worth including debt?
quiz.a: J.P. Morgan advised Strathcona (Jefferies its special committee); total value is about $2.7–2.9B including ~$550M of net debt.

chat.a: Monday was a rough session: the S&P 500 fell 1.9% to 7,417 and the Nasdaq 2.5%, led by Nvidia after its CEO's exit and new chip access limits on Chinese customers. The VIX rose to 22.91. Rates are still the backdrop, with the 10-year at 5.12%.

chat.q: What's your read on oil this week?
chat.a: Brent settled at $92.44 and WTI at $85.72, down about 3.5% and 3.2%, as recovering Hormuz shipments reinforce a surplus view. OPEC+ meets 29 Nov on 2027 output, which is the next catalyst. Lower prices help refiners and consumers but weigh on upstream asset valuations.

ECP closed its EnergySolutions buyout on 16 Nov, with Morgan Stanley and RBC advising EnergySolutions. Strathcona is buying Greenfire for about $2.7–2.9B including debt, and NRG is selling six gas plants to LS Power for $4B at about 8.0x 2027 EBITDA, advised by Barclays.
chat.tip: Name the advisers; bankers will ask.

chat.q: What are you watching this week?
chat.a: Nvidia earnings after the close on 17 Nov, since the stock has been the main drag on tech. Also October retail sales that day and the FOMC minutes on the 18th, which I want to read for how committed the Fed is to a December hike.
chat.tip: Tie each event to rates or AI spending.

chat.q: If the 10-year rose 50 bp, what happens to a DCF?
chat.a: The 10-year is 5.12% now. A 50 bp rise lifts the risk-free rate and so the WACC, which lowers the present value of cash flows. Long-duration assets with most of their value in the terminal value are hit hardest.
chat.tip: Say the direction, then who is hit hardest.

chat.q: How does a stock sell-off affect a deal like a sponsor buyout of EnergySolutions?
chat.a: Falling public multiples and a VIX of 22.91 make sellers and buyers less certain on price, but sponsor deals depend mainly on debt cost and availability. High yield spreads were 323 bp on 13 Nov, so credit is open, though the 10-year at 5.12% makes the all-in cost high.
chat.tip: Separate equity volatility from credit access.

chat.q: How do the Fed and the 10-year affect M&A financing right now?
chat.a: The Fed range is 3.75–4.00% after a September hike, and markets priced about 89% odds of another 25 bp in December as of 12 Nov. The 10-year is 5.12%, so debt is costly, but spreads near 323 bp mean credit is still available at a price.
chat.tip: Separate the base rate from the credit spread.
